Infancy means the earliest, most undeveloped stage of something. That "something" can be a human life, or it can be anything else — a company, a technology, an idea, a movement. The word always points to a beginning that is fragile, new, and still growing.
Meaning 1: The Earliest Stage of a Human Life

In its most direct and literal sense, infancy refers to the period of a person's life right after birth — roughly from birth up to around 1 to 2 years of age, though in casual usage people sometimes stretch it to mean the first few years before a child can speak or think independently.

During infancy, a person is called an infant. An infant is completely helpless and dependent on others for everything — feeding, warmth, movement, protection. They cannot speak, cannot walk, and cannot take care of themselves in any way. It is the most vulnerable and dependent phase of a human life.

"The doctor monitored the child's health carefully during infancy."
"Many habits and emotional patterns are shaped during infancy."

Think of infancy as the time when a person exists but has almost no ability to act on the world around them. They are alive, but just barely beginning.
Meaning 2: The Very Early Stage of Anything (Figurative Use)

This is the meaning you will encounter far more often in modern English. Infancy is widely used to describe the early, undeveloped stage of anything — not just human life. This is called a figurative (or metaphorical) use, meaning the word is borrowed from its original human-life meaning and applied more broadly.

The logic is simple: just as a human infant is new, undeveloped, weak, and full of potential, any new thing — a technology, a field of science, an industry, a political movement — can also be described as being in its infancy.

"In the 1990s, the internet was still in its infancy."
"Artificial intelligence, though powerful today, was in its infancy just a few decades ago."
"The company is still in its infancy and has a long way to go before it becomes profitable."
"The field of modern psychology was in its infancy in the late 1800s."

When you say something is "in its infancy," you are saying:

  • It is new and just getting started.
  • It is not yet fully formed or mature.
  • It has a lot of room to grow, improve, and develop.
  • It may be promising, but it hasn't reached its full potential yet.

This phrase — "in its infancy" — is one of the most common and important expressions built from this word. Memorize it, and you'll recognize it everywhere.

In law, particularly in older legal writing and some formal legal systems today, infancy refers to the state of being a minor — that is, a person who has not yet reached the legal age of adulthood (typically 18 years old, though this varies by country and context).

This legal meaning is broader than the everyday one. A 15-year-old is legally still in a state of "infancy" in this context, even though in everyday speech we would never call a teenager an infant.

In legal writing, you might see:

"The contract was void because one party was in a state of infancy at the time of signing."

This simply means the person was under the legal age of adulthood and therefore could not be legally bound by a contract. You won't encounter this meaning in everyday conversation, but it's good to know it exists so you're not confused if you ever read it in a legal document.
The Single Most Important Phrase to Know

If you remember nothing else, remember this:

"In its infancy"

This phrase means: at a very early, undeveloped stage. It is used all the time in journalism, academic writing, business, technology writing, and everyday conversation. Almost any time you see the word "infancy," it will appear inside this phrase.

"Infancy" is generally a neutral-to-positive word. It does not imply failure or weakness in a harsh way. Instead, it acknowledges that something is young and undeveloped while also hinting at future potential. When someone says a technology is "in its infancy," they are not insulting it — they are simply saying it is early, and the best is possibly yet to come.

ContextWhat "infancy" means

To pull it all together: infancy as a noun means the earliest, most undeveloped stage — of a human life (roughly birth to age 1–2), of anything new and not yet mature (figurative use), or of being legally under the age of adulthood (legal use). The figurative use is by far the most common in modern English, and the phrase "in its infancy" is the form you will see most often. The word always carries the idea of newness, fragility, potential, and incompleteness.
